THE III ADDL.
SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MEMBER MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIM TRIBUNAL NO.XII, VIJAYAPURA.

AND ALLOW THIS APPEAL TO GRANT THE COMPENSATION AMOUNT BY RS.14,99,000/- ONLY AS CLAIMED BY THE APPELLANT BEFORE THIS HON'BLE COURT,
 THESE APPEALS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT XII at Vijayapur (for short 'Tribunal) in MVC Nos.181/2015 and 182/2015, vide its common judgment and award dated 04.06.2019.

sentences.text: 2. The claimants were injured in a road traffic accident on 12.08.2014 when a bus belonging to the respondent/Corporation bearing registration No.MH-40/N-8329 dashed against two jeeps bearing registration Nos.MH-13/B- NC: 2023:KHC-K:5511 2196 and MH-13/B-9391 which they were driving.
The claimant in MVC N.181/2015 suffered compound injury of the left foot and tendons of foot and great toe was exposed apart from other injuries on right thigh, leg and arm.
The clamant in MVC No.182/2015 suffered two fractures of the 7th and 8th ribs of left side chest.
The claimants were treated as in patients.
They claimed that both of them were drivers by profession and earning Rs.8,000/- per month and due to the injuries, they were out of employment.
Hence, they filed separate clam petitions claiming compensation from the Corporation.

3. The claim petitions were opposed by the respondent/Corporation contending that the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 had parked his jeep on the wrong side while another jeep driven by the claimant in MVC No.182/2015 was driven in a rash and negligent manner.
It claimed that there was no fault on the part of the driver of the bus.
It denied the averments of the claim petitions as well as entitlement of the claimants for compensation.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petitions were taken up for trial.

The claimants were examined as PWs.1 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5511 and 2 and a doctor was examined as PW.3, who deposed that the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 had suffered disability to the extent of 12% to 15% to the left foot.
However, the claimant in MVC No.182/2015 did not examine any doctor to assess his disability.
They marked Exs.P1 to P18.
The Corporation did not lead any evidence.

5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 had suffered a compound injury due to which the tendon of the left foot and great toe Sharaddanand vs The Divisional Controller on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64323877/
3 was exposed.
It also noticed that the claimant in MVC No.182/2015 had suffered fracture of 7th and 8th ribs of left side chest.
The Tribunal therefore considered the disability suffered by the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 at 14% to the whole body and the claimant in MVC No.182/2015 suffered disability at 3% to the whole body.
It considered the age of the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 at 45 years while the claimant in MVC No.182/2015 was considered at 44 years.

The Tribunal considered the notional income of both the claimants at Rs.6,000/- per month and awarded the following compensation:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:5511 Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-
Medical expenses/bill Rs.30,000/-
Loss of earning during laid up period Rs.3,000/-
Loss of future earning on account of Rs.40,320/-
permanent disability Loss of amenities and future Rs.10,000/-
unhappiness Attendant, diet, conveyance and Rs.3,000/-
other charges Award amount on permanent Nil disability Total Rs.1,11,320/-
Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-
Medical expenses/bill Rs.20,000/-
Loss of earning during laid up period Rs.1,000/-
Loss of future earning on account of Rs.30,250/-
permanent disability Loss of amenities and future Rs.10,000/-
unhappiness Attendant, diet, conveyance and Rs.1,000/-
other charges Award amount on permanent Nil disability Total Rs.72,250/-
6.
The Tribunal directed the Corporation to pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petitions till the date of realization.

Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the Sharaddanand vs The Divisional Controller on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64323877/
4 claimants are in appeal.
The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 had suffered injuries apart from the compound injury on the left foot and great toe.
He submitted that assessment of disability by the Tribunal was not just and proper having regard to the injuries.
Likewise, he submitted that the claimant in MVC No.182/2015 had suffered two fracture of 7th and 8th ribs and taking into consideration his avocation, the Tribunal must have assessed the disability.

He further contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month while in similar circumstances the income must have been considered at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.
He therefore prayed that the compensation determined by the Tribunal be reconsidered and just compensation be awarded.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation on the other hand contended that the claimants did not suffer any fractures and therefore, they did not suffer any disability.
However, he did not dispute the fact that the claimants have suffered injuries in the accident and that they were treated as inpatients in hospitals.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants as well as the learned counsel for the respondent/Corporation.

10. Having regard to the fact that the claimant in MVC No.181/2015 had suffered a compound injury and great toe was exposed and claimant in MVC No.182/2015 had suffered two fractures of 7th and 8th ribs of left side chest, this Court considers it appropriate to enhance the compensation globally awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.181/2015 at a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- and in MVC No.182/2015 at a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.

This would meet the ends of justice as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is meager and this would also cover the difference in the loss of earning during laid up period by considering the notional income at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month as well as loss income due to disability.
11. In that view of the matter, both these appeals are allowed in part and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MVC No.181/2015 is enhanced from Rs1,11,320/- to a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-.

Likewise, the compensation of Rs.72,250/- awarded in MVC No.182/2015 is enhanced to a sum of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5511 Rs.1,00,000/-, which is payable by the respondent/Corporation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petitions till the date of realization excluding the delayed period 202 and 185 days respectively in filing these appeals.

12. The enhanced compensation along with interest shall be deposited by the Corporation before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and award.
